data.title: bn-1wj: M1.5.2.2 Rounds: canaries, step intents, sends, flow read-back and identity probes

data.body: [HIGH] The plant operation is not compiled/fail-closed:  records the compiled POST URL, but the macro path passes only the mutable Teapot macro name/session/edits to . Neither the registry nor preflight binds the macro bytes/digest, and the readback URL/method comparison happens only after dispatch. Disposable exact-target regression: replacing the one-request macro URL with the same in-scope  still dispatched and retained that request; acquisition then returned  and persisted . Thus a changed macro can cause an effect different from the durable intent before detection, violating the trusted compiled grammar and intent-before-effect contract. Bind and verify the exact macro/request grammar before any dispatch (including body/headers), or generate the request directly from compiled code; add a regression proving drift is refused with zero target sends.

[HIGH] The registered request ceiling is lower than the execution it admits. The recipe loop counts C as one authenticated send, but  dispatches two authenticated DELETE actions for C, so one round can need 35 sends (login+request+retry for 11 authenticated actions, plus F0/F3), not the asserted 32. More broadly, preflight has no round count while public  can execute N rounds against that fixed one-round admission. Disposable regression changed the existing FakeServices expectation to 35 and failed . Derive the count from the same compiled action registry used by execution, multiply/check it against the admitted round count with overflow protection, and add drift/multi-round ceiling regressions.

[HIGH correction with exact identifiers] RequestAction records the compiled POST URL, but teapot_dispatch calls replay_macro with only macro_name, session and edits. The registry and preflight bind no macro bytes or digest; URL and method are checked only after dispatch. Disposable exact-target regression changed the registered one-request macro URL to /app/api/orders?macro-drift=1. It dispatched and retained that URL, then acquire_rounds returned ReadbackMismatch and the P step persisted Effect::Unknown. A mutable macro can therefore cause an effect different from the durable intent before detection. Bind and verify exact macro/request grammar before dispatch, including body and headers, or generate the request directly from compiled code; prove drift is refused with zero sends.

[HIGH correction with exact identifiers] registered_execution_plan counts C once, while acquire_rounds dispatches two authenticated DELETE actions for C. One round can need 35 sends, not the currently asserted 32. Preflight also has no round-count input, while execute_live accepts arbitrary round_count against this fixed admission. Disposable regression changed the existing FakeServices required_requests expectation to 35; the exact focused test failed with left 32, right 35. Derive the ceiling from the same compiled action registry, bind it to round_count with checked arithmetic, and cover cleanup drift plus multi-round admission.

data.reason: Two HIGH blockers: mutable macro grammar can dispatch an effect different from the persisted compiled intent before readback detects drift; preflight admits 32 sends for a one-round execution that needs up to 35 and is not bound to round_count. See open threads th-1oktjc and th-3tu74h with disposable regressions.

data.body: Fixed in 1a847b8: P/P2 now use only the exact compiled direct Teapot send (POST, registered collection URL, Content-Type, canonical JSON canary body) serialized in the durable intent before dispatch; macro replay was removed from execution. The pinned live regression installs a hostile DELETE macro and still completes the exact cross-user readback with no macro traffic.

Fixed in 1a847b8: one shared compiled dispatch table now drives execution cardinality and checked admission at 35*N, including P/P2, all four identity sends, all treatments, two anonymous sends, and both authenticated cleanup DELETEs. round_count is bound into the private Prepared plan and execute_live no longer accepts caller N; 1-round, 3-round, zero, and overflow regressions pass.

data.reason: Retarget regression: a 35*N plan above the frozen Count range reaches adapters before refusal

data.body: Retarget 1a847b8 fixes 35-per-round cardinality and binds N, but the pre-adapter refusal is still incomplete. operations.rs:287-298 accepts every multiplication that fits u64; preflight.rs:540-545 therefore constructs a plan when required_requests exceeds the frozen JSON Count limit of 2^53-1. The only range check is accounting.rs:313-315, inside LiveServices.admit after verifier_preflight and begin_accounting have already invoked Teapot. Disposable exact-target regression: set N=(MAX_SAFE_INTEGER/35)+1 (257348550135457), expect RoundCount and zero service calls. Actual: prepare returns Ok with required_requests=9007199254740995 and FakeServices.admit runs. cargo test -p scourge-core compiled_budget_binds_n_rounds_and_refuses_zero_or_overflow_before_admission fails at unwrap_err on that Prepared value. Reject required_requests above MAX_SAFE_INTEGER in registered_execution_plan before locks or adapters, and retain this boundary regression.

Verified fixed at exact target 1a847b8. P and P2 now construct compiled POST send actions to the registered collection with exact application/json header and canonical BTreeMap body; RequestIntent persists and hashes method, URL, session, headers, and body before dispatch. teapot_dispatch has no replay branch and invokes only Teapot send from that bound action. The hostile live regression installs a mutable DELETE macro yet the pinned one-round acquisition succeeds with 13 retained byte-backed flows, proving the macro is passive-only and cannot alter plant dispatch. Focused round tests also pass 8/8 including intent/SIGKILL, nonreuse and grammar tests. Leaving this thread resolved.

data.reason: Exact target 1a847b8 remains blocked: 35*N plans above the frozen JSON Count range but below u64 overflow reach Teapot adapters before CountOutOfRange refusal; see reopened th-3tu74h and its failing disposable boundary regression.

data.body: Fixed in 79454ca: registered_execution_plan now rejects round_count, requests_per_round, or required_requests outside the same 2^53-1 canonical Count domain before lock acquisition or services.admit. The exact maximum admitted N=257348550135456 (total 9007199254740960) passes; N=257348550135457 (total 9007199254740995), MAX_SAFE+1, u64::MAX, and zero all return RoundCount with FakeServices calls empty and no conflicts held.

data.body: Verified fixed at exact target 79454ca. registered_execution_plan rejects zero, round_count above 2^53-1, and required_requests above 2^53-1 before lock_inputs, lock acquisition, conflict claims, or services.admit. The exact target regression admits N=257348550135456 with 35*N=9007199254740960, while N+1, MAX_SAFE+1, u64::MAX, and zero return RoundCount with FakeServices calls empty and no conflicts held. Non-vacuity mutation removing only the required_requests bound made N+1 return Prepared with acquired locks, so the regression kills the missing-bound bug. A disposable production accounting probe also admitted 9007199254740960 and canonical AccountingV1 round-tripped that exact u64 without overflow or truncation. Focused test and full gates pass. Leaving resolved.

Confirmed unchanged and still covered at exact target 79454ca. The only new source changes are the preflight range guard and its regression; rounds execution still has no replay_macro or run_macro call path. Focused rounds pass 8/8 and the pinned hostile DELETE macro live round passes with direct compiled P/P2 dispatch. Leaving resolved.
